title: Discussion night Session #131: Civic Tech x IOG Policy Crunch
speaker: Lucas Cherkewski
description_markdown:
To change things up in May, we’re co-hosting the Institute on Governance (IOG) Policy Crunch event, “The future of digital governance in a post-pandemic world”. See the end of this Meetup invite for the full description.
Register for this free event through IOG here: https://iog.ca/events/digital-governance-post-pandemic/ (*be sure to register through IOG to get the videoconference login provided to you the day of the event)

==============
Speaking:

- Jaimie Boyd (Chief Digital Officer, Government of British Columbia)

- David Eaves (Lecturer of Public Policy, Harvard Kennedy School)

- Jesse Hirsh (President, Metaviews.ca)

- Shingai Manjengwa (CEO Fireside Analytics & Technical Education Specialist, Vector Institute)
Moderator: Ryan Androsoff (Director of Digital Leadership Program, Institute on Governance)
==============
Agenda:
17:30-18:00 EST - Log-in to videoconferencing system and virtual intros and networking
18:00-19:00 EST - Policy Crunch panel discussion with audience Q&A
19:00-19:30 EST - Ottawa Civic Tech presentation and discussion
==============
Event description:
Our world has changed dramatically in the past few weeks as a result of the unprecedented COVID-19 pandemic. Governments have been in crisis mode responding to the immediate health and economic impacts of the pandemic, while at the same time seeing many of their processes and operations disrupted by the need to work, collaborate, and deliver services in a fully digital way like never before.
Once the immediate crisis has passed, the question remains as to what long-term changes to government and society will we see as a result? Will the "new normal" of the post-pandemic world see digital government efforts be accelerated with employees continuing to work remotely and services increasingly delivered online? This Policy Crunch will explore these issues and the impact that the pandemic response is having on related topics such as privacy and cyber security, the use of AI and data analytics, and the skills and competencies needed for government and citizens to effectively engage in a digital world.
This will be IOG's first fully online Policy Crunch as we follow current social distancing guidelines. Please register via Eventbrite on the IOG event page and login details and instructions for our videoconference platform will be sent to you in advance of the session. A live stream of the proceedings will also be available on YouTube and archived for later access, similar to regular practice for Policy Crunch events.

title: Hacknight Session #112: Linkable Open Data Environment
speaker: Matthew Darwin
description_markdown:
Alessandro Alasia from Statistics Canada's Data Exploration and Integration Lab (DEIL) will present on progress towards building a Linkable Open Data Environment.
Over the last few years, the DEIL has conducted an increasing amount of work with open data using various open source tools in an open ecosystem. This exploration and experience has given rise to the idea of using an “open project” approach. In this session, Alessandro will present examples and outcomes of “open projects” at DEIL, that is, projects that, to the extent possible, make use of open software, open code, open standards, open data, and open project management tools. It also outlines how DEIL is now exploring integration of open databases through the development of a Linkable Open Data Environment (LODE).
To date, achievements include the completion of openly licensed databases of virtually all building footprints across Canada, in collaboration with Microsoft, and preliminary versions of open databases of business, educational facilities, hospitals and addresses. Further, these open databases are providing insights on the potential of data value multiplication through stakeholder use and enrichment of the original baseline datasets.

title: Speculative Civic Tech Futures: Hacknight Session #98
speaker: Douglas Vidal-Hernandez
description_markdown:
Ottawa Civic Tech and Speculative Futures Ottawa invite you to a special event for our 98th hacknight session. As technology becomes increasingly accessible and open for citizens to contribute to within their civic environment, how can we build our future cities together? What is the role of creativity and imagination in the context of civic tech and policy design? What are the narratives we are creating for our shared futures as we develop technologies that are for the public good? How will the environment we live in shape new technologies and vice versa?
Join our 3 panellists on December 11th at Impact Hub Ottawa.
------
Remco Volmer, Artengine
Remco is the managing director of Artengine, Ottawa's lab for creative technology. A graduate of Utrecht University of Art’s Creative Media program, he has focused his practice on technologically mediated interaction design. As a cultural producer, he has organized a variety of exhibitions and festivals, including the Electric Fields festival of electronic art and Maker Faire Ottawa. He has a strong interest in innovation in the arts, both on the individual level of the artist and on the combined level of the institution.
------
Natale Dankotuwage, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
Born and raised in the Greater Toronto Area, Natale Dankotuwage is an Undergraduate from University of Toronto in Political Science and a Master’s Graduate from Ontario College of Art and Design in Strategic Foresight and Innovation.
As a Social Innovator, she has worked on post-war development with the Asia Foundation. And has worked as a community manager of co-working spaces for digital tech entrepreneurs in Bangalore India and Toronto, Canada. These days she is a Federal Public Servant working for the Government of Canada on digital innovation. Her passion for social innovation persists. She was a Global Ambassador at the 2018 Unleashed Global Innovation Summit in Singapore.
Change-making has been a passion of hers for years. Believing we all have the potential to make a positive difference in our communities, nation and world.
------
Tom Baynes, Policy Horizons Canada
Tom is an intellectual adventurer with a background in anthropology, art history, and public administration, connecting intangible aspects of human experience to concrete social policy issues. He strives to show the value of qualitative research methods in making informed choices about the future, and translate humanistic perspectives into usable insights. At home, his neuroticism and intellectual perversity are seen in his passion for textile crafts, bad television, great movies, and books on aesthetics, social theory, and cultural history.
------

Join us and be part of this important conversation and relationship between government and citizens. You do not need to be a "techie" to attend --everyone is welcome, and everyone can contribute questions, ideas, and insights on how we might work with government changemakers to build civic good through technology, data, design, policy, advocacy & citizen engagement.

This month's guest speakers are Beverley Gibas and Robert Giggey from the City of Ottawa who will be introducing a new Open311 Web Services Pilot to the Ottawa Civic Tech community:
To support the City of Ottawa’s Strategic Objective to improve access to City services through digital service delivery, the City is launching an application program interface (API) that will allow the external community to develop applications that can submit Service Requests directly to the City as well as to consume data regarding these Service Requests. Officials from the Chief Information Officer Branch of the Government of Canada’s Treasury Board Secretariat are engaging with stakeholders across Canada on the topic of Digital Government. These discussions are an opportunity to exchange ideas and suggestions to shape a ‘made in Canada’ approach to digital government as they work to improve how digital services are delivered to citizens. The discussions will touch several major themes, including:
– Organizing to deliver digital government, and what we can learn from other jurisdictions and organizations
– Digital talent in government, and how we can bring in world-class digital expertise
– Digital service design and delivery, and how to build services from a user-centred perspective
– Setting the foundations for digital government capacity, building on the federal government’s IT Strategic Plan and Cloud Adoption Strategy
Les fonctionnaires de la Direction du dirigeant principal de l’information du Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor du gouvernement du Canada mobilisent les principaux intervenants des quatre coins du pays sur le sujet du gouvernement numérique. Ces discussions représentent une occasion d’échanger vos idées et de faire des suggestions afin de forger une approche « fabriquée au Canada » en matière de gouvernement numérique, de même que de proposer une façon d’améliorer la prestation des services numériques à l’endroit des citoyens. Ces discussions aborderont plusieurs thèmes majeurs, y compris :
– Organisation en vue du déploiement du gouvernement numérique, et ce que nous pouvons apprendre de l’expérience acquise par d’autres organisations et administrations gouvernementales.
– Talent numérique au sein du gouvernement, et comment nous pouvons attirer des compétences spécialisées de classe mondiale.
– Conception et mise en œuvre de services numériques, et comment élaborer des services du point de vue de l’utilisateur.
– Établissement des bases adéquates pour assurer la capacité du gouvernement numérique, et comment miser sur le Plan stratégique de la technologie de l’information et sur la Stratégie d’adoption de l’informatique en nuage du gouvernement du Canada.
